## INIT2 · INIT2-failure-status-and-unsafe — INIT2: a system-failure power-off kind, and one unsafe in init's binary

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Evidence: Ruled: (A) option (1), system_reset kind 3 (power off reporting SystemFailure) added by INIT2 in the kernel, libs/sys and devices.md with the Architect's sentence; refusals judge poweroff_status 255. (D) no unsafe in init: libs/rt's _start for the bundle's first program gives main a &'static [u8] view, one SAFETY-documented unsafe in start.rs, rt's budget 11 -&gt; 12; init stays at 0 with forbid(unsafe_code) on the binary. Forwarded to INIT2's implementer; checked at review.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `ebf2ae7c237b4800585de6ed646db856` · 2026-10-03T01:00:18Z

> Two of INIT2's deliverable-2 gaps are yours (the other two, the bound counting one exit-watch thread per server priced from objects.md, and init's own badge as the smallest unused at each endpoint, I accepted). (A) Ruling 4 has a refusal power off 'with the system-failure status' (QEMU exit 255, SBI SRST reason 1), but system_reset on devices.md has only kind 1 power off and 2 reboot with reason 'no reason', so no call gives 255. Options: (1) the kernel adds kind 3, power off with system failure (SBI reason 1): kernel, libs/sys, devices.md, about ten lines, in K16's crates but not its lines; (2) refusal cases judge by init's refusal line and exit 0, ruling 4's status dropped. The implementer recommends (1) and offers to do it with leave; I agree, with whoever merges second rebasing. Your ruling and the devices.md line. (D) The stub's bytes: embedded with a build.rs as tests/programs does; the bundle reader a safe module in init's lib with host tests; but the binary needs one documented unsafe to view the loader's mapping, so init's unsafe budget goes 0 -> 1. Is one unsafe in init acceptable, or does libs/rt's startup-page view (already counted there) give init the mapping safely? The implementer builds refusals with kind 1 meanwhile and switches when (A) lands.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `dfc5afd7466cf46968a8067c45a3188c` · 2026-10-03T01:01:20Z

> (A) Option (1). Ruling 4 stands. A refused boot ends the same way whoever refuses it. boot.md R17 (fail closed) has every loader and kernel refusal power off through SRST with SystemFailure, and the bench reads that as status 255. An init refusal that exits 0 could not be told apart from a clean shutdown. INIT2 adds `kind` 3 in the kernel, libs/sys (the decode's tag list and its host test) and devices.md, and whoever merges second rebases.
> 
> devices.md "`system_reset`": replace the first sentence ("`system_reset(h(Reset), kind)` powers the machine off (`kind` 1) or reboots it (`kind` 2) through the firmware's system reset call.") with:
> > `system_reset(h(Reset), kind)` powers the machine off (`kind` 1), reboots it (`kind` 2), or powers it off reporting a system failure (`kind` 3), through the firmware's system reset call; only `kind` 3 gives the firmware a reason, `SystemFailure`. `init` refuses a boot with `kind` 3, as the loader and the kernel refuse one ([R17 (fail closed)](boot.md#r17-fail-closed)).
> The Errors sentence stays. The status line names the refusal cases that ask for `poweroff_status = 255` as `kind` 3's test.
> 
> (D) No unsafe in init. TENETS ("`unsafe` is a budget": few, small modules with safe interfaces) puts this view in libs/rt, next to the startup page's. Both rest on the same invariant: pages the loader or the parent mapped read-only for the life of the process. rt gets an entry for the bundle's first program, whose `_start` takes the bundle's address and length (`a0`, `a1`; boot.md "The loader loads only the kernel and `init`") and gives `main` a `&'static [u8]`. Its one SAFETY-documented unsafe goes in start.rs. rt's budget goes 11 -> 12, and its name line adds "the bundle's view". init stays at 0, with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` on the binary as on the library. rt-miri covers the parse side as it does today. Building refusals with kind 1 until (A) lands is fine, as long as no case is accepted judging exit 0.
